status: drafted via lean single-pass workflow grounded in the real extracted verse text
notes: Read the full Ethiopian-translation text (6 chapters, 113 verses) directly and compared verse-by-verse against the already-completed KJV 1Timothy.json structure — the content is textually identical to KJV across every chapter (same pastoral-letter shape: Paul's testimony/charge to Timothy, fables/genealogies, prayer for rulers, women's church conduct, bishop/deacon qualifications, the Mystery of Godliness creed, latter-day apostasy, widows, elders, servants, love of money). No real content differences found (unlike this same translation's Ezra, which genuinely diverges) — so the KJV's 13-tier structure (2 person tiers + 11 law/theme tiers) was adapted rather than invented from scratch, with every verse reference re-verified against this translation's own text and every id re-scoped with an _ethiopian suffix to avoid collision with the KJV entries. As with KJV: no separate Jesus tier (Christ is referenced only doctrinally — one Mediator 2:5, manifest in the flesh 3:16, witnessed before Pilate 6:13 — never an acting character in this letter). Naming-collision flag carried over: Hymenaeus/Alexander (1:20) are not asserted to be the same men who reappear in 2 Timothy. Pontius Pilate (6:13) logged in genealogyLists only, as a historical reference point, not an active character in this book.

scribeTiers.scribeName: Doctrines of Devils in the Latter Times

characters.name: Paul the Apostle

verses.note: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the commandment of God our Saviour, writes to Timothy, 'my own son in the faith,' with grace, mercy, and peace.
Recounts having besought Timothy to abide still at Ephesus when Paul went into Macedonia, to charge some that they teach no other doctrine.

Paul's personal testimony: was before a blasphemer, persecutor, and injurious, but obtained mercy because he did it ignorantly in unbelief; the grace of the Lord was exceeding abundant; Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom Paul is chief, showing forth all longsuffering for a pattern to believers.
Doxology following his testimony: 'Now unto the King eternal, immortal, invisible, the only wise God, be honour and glory for ever and ever. Amen.'
Commits this charge to Timothy according to the prophecies which went before on him; names Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom he has delivered unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme.
Exhorts that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgiving be made for all men; states he was ordained a preacher, an apostle, and a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and verity.
Writes these things hoping to come to Timothy shortly, but in case he tarries long, so Timothy may know how to behave himself in the house of God.
Instructs Timothy to put the brethren in remembrance of these things, to command and teach them, and to give attendance to reading, exhortation, and doctrine till Paul comes.
Final closing charge: O Timothy, keep that which is committed to thy trust, avoiding profane and vain babblings, and oppositions of science falsely so called.

funFacts: Paul's self-description as formerly 'a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious' (1:13) is consistent across this translation and KJV.

characters.name: Timothy

genealogy.father: unnamed Greek father — Acts 16:1, not itself part of this book's text
genealogy.mother: Eunice — 2 Timothy 1:5, not individually indexed in this book

verses.note: Addressed by Paul as 'my own son in the faith.'
Besought by Paul to abide still at Ephesus, to charge certain men that they teach no other doctrine.
This charge is committed to Timothy according to the prophecies which went before on him, that he might war a good warfare.
Told to let no man despise his youth, but to be an example of the believers in word, conversation, charity, spirit, faith, purity.

Told to give attendance to reading, exhortation, and doctrine till Paul comes; not to neglect the gift given him by prophecy with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery; to meditate on these things and take heed to himself and the doctrine.
Instructed how to treat elder men, younger men, elder women, and younger women within the church, as fathers, brothers, mothers, sisters, with all purity.
Told to drink no longer water only, but to use a little wine for his stomach's sake and his often infirmities.

Called 'O man of God' and charged to flee covetous things, follow righteousness, and fight the good fight of faith, keeping the commandment without spot until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ; closes with a doxology to the King eternal.
Final address: 'O Timothy, keep that which is committed to thy trust.'

funFacts: 1 Timothy 4:14 references 'the gift that is in thee...given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery,' generally understood as Timothy's own ordination.

verses.note: Named as examples of those who, having put away faith and a good conscience, made shipwreck concerning the faith; Paul says he has delivered them unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme. The text groups them together without differentiating individual actions, indexed as one collective entry — not asserted to be the same men named in 2 Timothy.

characters.name: Fables and Endless Genealogies
characters.purpose: Warns against speculative teaching — fables and genealogical disputes that minister questions rather than godly edifying — and the misuse of the law, bookended by the same warning at the letter's close.

verses.note: Charge that some teach no other doctrine, neither give heed to fables and endless genealogies, which minister questions rather than godly edifying which is in faith.

The end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart, a good conscience, and faith unfeigned; some have swerved and turned aside unto vain jangling, desiring to be teachers of the law, understanding neither what they say nor whereof they affirm.
The law is good if a man use it lawfully, knowing it is not made for a righteous man but for the lawless and disobedient, according to the glorious gospel committed to Paul's trust.
Closing echo: avoid profane and vain babblings, and oppositions of science falsely so called, which some professing have erred concerning the faith.

characters.name: Prayers, Supplications, and Intercessions
characters.purpose: Instructs the church to pray broadly, including for kings and civil authority, grounded in God's universal will to save and Christ's role as the one mediator between God and men.

verses.note: Exhorts that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks be made for all men, for kings and all in authority, that believers may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty.
Good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour, who will have all men to be saved and come unto the knowledge of the truth.
There is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus, who gave himself a ransom for all, to be testified in due time.
Paul states he is ordained a preacher, apostle, and teacher of the Gentiles in faith and verity; men are to pray everywhere, lifting up holy hands, without wrath and doubting.

characters.name: The Woman's Adornment and Silence
characters.purpose: Sets instructions for women's dress and conduct in the gathered church, grounded in the Genesis creation and fall order — Adam formed first, then Eve, and Eve deceived.

verses.note: Women to adorn themselves in modest apparel, with shamefacedness and sobriety, not with broided hair, gold, pearls, or costly array, but with good works, as becometh women professing godliness.
Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection; not suffered to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence.
For Adam was first formed, then Eve; Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression.
Notwithstanding she shall be saved in childbearing, if they continue in faith and charity and holiness with sobriety.

characters.name: The Bishop's Qualifications
characters.purpose: Lists the moral character and household qualifications required of anyone who desires the office of a bishop.

verses.note: If a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work.

A bishop must be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behaviour, given to hospitality, apt to teach; not given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre, but patient, not a brawler, not covetous.
One that ruleth well his own house, having his children in subjection with all gravity; for if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?
Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil; must have a good report of them which are without, lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.

characters.name: The Deacon's Qualifications
characters.purpose: Sets equivalent moral qualifications for deacons and their wives, the second recognized office of the church alongside the bishop.

verses.note: Deacons must be grave, not doubletongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre, holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience.
Let these also first be proved; then let them use the office of a deacon, being found blameless.
Their wives must likewise be grave, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things.

Deacons to be husbands of one wife, ruling their children and their own houses well; those who have used the office well purchase to themselves a good degree and great boldness in the faith which is in Christ Jesus.

characters.name: The Mystery of Godliness
characters.purpose: A short creedal statement summarizing the incarnation and proclamation of Christ, given as the theological center the church — 'the pillar and ground of the truth' — exists to uphold.

verses.note: Paul writes hoping to come to Timothy shortly, but in case he tarries long, so Timothy may know how to behave himself in the house of God, the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth.

Without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory.

characters.name: Doctrines of Devils in the Latter Times
characters.scribeTier: Doctrines of Devils in the Latter Times
characters.purpose: Warns of a coming falling-away marked by false asceticism — forbidding marriage, forbidding meats — countered by the teaching that every creature of God is good, and by a positive charge to refuse profane and old wives' fables and instead exercise unto godliness, since godliness profits both this life and the life to come.

verses.note: The Spirit speaketh expressly that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits and doctrines of devils, speaking lies in hypocrisy, having their conscience seared with a hot iron.
Forbidding to marry, and commanding to abstain from meats which God hath created to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth.
Every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving, for it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.

Charged to refuse profane and old wives' fables, and exercise himself rather unto godliness; bodily exercise profiteth little, but godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is and of that which is to come; Paul and his companions labour and suffer reproach because they trust in the living God, who is the Saviour of all men, specially of those that believe.

characters.name: The Widow Indeed
characters.purpose: Sets criteria for the church's care of widows and for enrolling certain widows into a recognized order of service, distinguishing genuine need (a 'widow indeed') from cases a widow's own family or remarriage should properly address.

verses.note: Honour widows that are widows indeed.
If a widow have children or nephews, let them learn first to shew piety at home, and to requite their parents; that is good and acceptable before God.
She that is a widow indeed, and desolate, trusteth in God, and continueth in supplications and prayers night and day; but she that liveth in pleasure is dead while she liveth.
These things give in charge, that they may be blameless — Timothy is told to command the preceding instructions.
If any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.

A widow taken into the number should not be under threescore years old, having been the wife of one man, well reported of for good works — bringing up children, lodging strangers, washing the saints' feet, relieving the afflicted, diligently following every good work.

The younger widows to be refused; when they wax wanton against Christ they will marry, having damnation because they have cast off their first faith, and learn to be idle, wandering from house to house, tattlers and busybodies.
Paul's counsel that the younger women marry, bear children, guide the house, give none occasion to the adversary, since some are already turned aside after Satan.
If any man or woman that believeth have widows, let them relieve them, and let not the church be charged, that it may relieve them that are widows indeed.

characters.name: Elders That Rule Well
characters.purpose: Sets protocol for honoring, correcting, and ordaining elders, guarding the process against favoritism and hasty judgment.

verses.note: Let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine.
For the scripture saith, Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn. And, The labourer is worthy of his reward.
Against an elder receive not an accusation, but before two or three witnesses.
Them that sin rebuke before all, that others also may fear.
Charges Timothy before God, the Lord Jesus Christ, and the elect angels, to observe these things without preferring one before another, doing nothing by partiality.
Lay hands suddenly on no man, neither be partaker of other men's sins; keep thyself pure.
Some men's sins are open beforehand, going before to judgment, and some men they follow after; likewise the good works of some are manifest beforehand, and they that are otherwise cannot be hid.

characters.name: Servants Under the Yoke
characters.purpose: Instructs Christian bondservants on honoring their masters, protecting the church's reputation and rightly valuing a believing master as a brother rather than presuming on the relationship.

verses.note: Let as many servants as are under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honour, that the name of God and his doctrine be not blasphemed.
They that have believing masters, let them not despise them because they are brethren, but rather do them service, because they are faithful and beloved, partakers of the benefit.

characters.name: The Love of Money
characters.purpose: Warns against false teachers who suppose gain is godliness, and instructs both the discontented — that godliness with contentment is itself great gain — and the already-rich, to be generous rather than trust in uncertain riches.

verses.note: If any man teach otherwise, and consent not to wholesome words of our Lord Jesus Christ and the doctrine according to godliness, he is proud, knowing nothing, doting about questions and strifes of words, whereof cometh envy, strife, railings, evil surmisings, perverse disputings of men of corrupt minds, supposing that gain is godliness: from such withdraw thyself.
Godliness with contentment is great gain; we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out; having food and raiment let us be therewith content.

They that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts; the love of money is the root of all evil, which some coveting after have erred from the faith and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.
Charge them that are rich in this world that they be not highminded, nor trust in uncertain riches, but in the living God, who giveth us richly all things to enjoy.

That they do good, that they be rich in good works, ready to distribute, willing to communicate; laying up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come, that they may lay hold on eternal life.

genealogyLists.note: Bulk or deliberately-unresolved references, kept out of the character list above.

pontius_pilate_reference.note: Christ Jesus is described as having 'before Pontius Pilate witnessed a good confession' — cited only as a historical reference point within Timothy's 6:11-16 charge, not as an active character in this book; no separate character entry made.

timothy_family_background.note: Timothy's father (unnamed Greek), mother (Eunice), and grandmother (Lois) are described elsewhere in scripture but not within 1 Timothy itself; noted for completeness, not indexed as separate characters here.
